resource.name: AccessModelTrack
resource.title: CMS ACCESS Model Clinical Track
resource.description: The four clinical tracks of the CMS ACCESS Model. Used to scope PlanDefinitions, ChargeItemDefinitions, and billing ActivityDefinitions to a single track.

concept.definition: Hypertension, dyslipidemia, obesity or overweight with a marker of central obesity, and prediabetes.
Diabetes, chronic kidney disease (stage 3a or 3b), and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, including heart disease.

resource.name: AccessModelTrackValueSet
resource.title: CMS ACCESS Model Clinical Tracks
resource.description: All four ACCESS Model clinical tracks.

resource.name: AccessModelTask
resource.title: CMS ACCESS Model Task Type
resource.description: Task types for operating the CMS ACCESS Model. Every ActivityDefinition in this bundle carries one of these codes, so Tasks generated from them can be searched with Task?code=.

concept.definition: Find the patient's MBI from demographics when it is not already on file. An MBI is required for every CMS eligibility check.
Run a CMS eligibility check and record Part A and Part B coverage, hospice election, ESRD, and primary payer status.
Confirm the patient carries a diagnosis that qualifies for the track. The qualifying diagnosis list is published by CMS and is not returned in an eligibility response.
Confirm through the CMS ACCESS Model APIs that the patient is aligned to this Participant for this track.
Confirm the rendering clinician is on the Participant's Clinician Roster registered with CMS.
Enroll the aligned patient onto the track and open the initial 12-month period.
Capture the track's outcome measures for the month. Outcome performance determines the variable 20 percent of the OAP.
Assemble and submit the monthly OAP claim. One service line, one unit of service, dated the first day ACCESS services were provided that month.
Reconcile the $0 ERA against the separate Outcome-Aligned Payment issued by CMS.

concept.display: Care update to the primary clinician
concept.definition: Send the monthly care update to the patient's primary care physician or referring clinician.
Primary or referring clinician reviews the ACCESS care update and performs at least one care-coordination activity.
Assemble and submit the CMP claim. Capped at three payments per patient, per track, every 12 months.
Move the patient from the initial-period G-code to the follow-on G-code at the 12-month mark.

resource.name: AccessMbiLookup
resource.title: Look up the patient's Medicare Beneficiary Identifier
resource.description: A Medicare Beneficiary Identifier is required for every CMS eligibility check. When the MBI is not on file, run an MBI lookup from demographics: name, date of birth, and optionally SSN. A successful lookup returns the same information as an eligibility response, including the MBI.

resource.name: AccessMedicareEligibilityCheck
resource.title: Run the CMS eligibility check
resource.description: Submit a CoverageEligibilityRequest to CMS and record four things from the response: active Part A and Part B coverage (benefit code 1 with insurance type MA and MB), hospice election periods (benefit code X, service type 45), end-stage renal disease (benefit code D, service type RN), and any other primary payer (benefit code R). An eligibility check cannot confirm full ACCESS eligibility.

resource.name: AccessQualifyingDiagnosisReview
resource.title: Confirm a qualifying diagnosis for the track
resource.description: Review the patient's Condition list against the qualifying diagnoses CMS publishes for this track. This is not returned in an eligibility response and has to be established from the chart.

resource.name: AccessAlignmentVerification
resource.title: Verify ACCESS alignment through the CMS ACCESS Model APIs
resource.description: Patients complete an alignment process that matches them to a specific ACCESS Participant. Confirm alignment through the CMS ACCESS Model APIs before opening a billing period. Without alignment the OAP claim is not payable.

resource.name: AccessClinicianRosterCheck
resource.title: Confirm the rendering clinician is on the Clinician Roster
resource.description: On an OAP claim the rendering provider must appear on the Participant's Clinician Roster registered with CMS, and the billing provider must use the Participant's Type 2 NPI.

resource.name: AccessPatientEnrollment
resource.title: Enroll the patient onto the ACCESS track
resource.description: Open the initial 12-month period for the patient on this track and record the enrollment date. The date of service on each monthly OAP claim is the first day ACCESS services were provided in that month.

resource.name: AccessRemittanceReconciliation
resource.title: Reconcile the $0 ERA against the OAP payment
resource.description: CMS does not pay OAP claims directly. The ERA shows a payment of $0 and the Outcome-Aligned Payment arrives separately. Post the ERA as acknowledgment that the claim was accepted, and reconcile the OAP against the month's accepted claims rather than against individual remittances.

resource.name: AccessPcpCareUpdate
resource.title: Send the monthly care update to the primary clinician
resource.description: Send the patient's progress and any recommended follow-up to their primary care physician or referring clinician. This update is what the clinician reviews to bill a Co-Management Payment.

coding.display: Care update to the primary clinician

resource.name: AccessComanagementReview
resource.title: Review the care update and perform a care-coordination activity
resource.description: The primary or referring clinician reviews the ACCESS Participant's care update and performs at least one care-coordination activity, such as documenting a follow-up action. Both are required before billing a CMP.

resource.name: AccessFollowonTransition
resource.title: Transition the patient to the follow-on period
resource.description: At the 12-month mark, close the initial period and open a follow-on period so monthly claims move to the follow-on G-code. The musculoskeletal track has no follow-on period.

resource.title: Submit the monthly OAP claim - Early cardio-kidney-metabolic, initial period (G0669)
resource.description: One professional claim per patient per month with a single service line: G0669, one unit of service, dated the first day ACCESS services were provided that month. Claims submitted more than 90 days after the date of service are not payable. Submit to the Medicare Administrative Contractor for the patient's jurisdiction, not to CMS directly.
